title: Microbatch hotpath telescoping — debug journal
content:
Summary:

This is my scratchpad while triaging the sudden throughput regression noticed on 2025-11-03 in the microbatching hotpath. Symptoms: sustained drop in tokens/sec for long-chat workloads (~30% below baseline), occasional 2–3x spike in tail p99 latency, and an increased occupancy on the prefill worker threads. The service does not fully OOM and CPU/GPU utilization stays within expected ranges — suggests queuing/packing/kvcache interactions rather than raw resource shortage.

Goals for this doc: chronicle commands tried, raw logs and error snippets, quick hypotheses, and short experiments to validate. Keep notes noisy — will prune later.

Observed timeline (high level):
- 2025-11-03 02:15 UTC: Internal synthetic load test (scale test rehearsal) starts hitting hosted cluster. Shortly after, net tokens/sec for model-x-4k drops from ~1.2M to ~780k.
- 2025-11-03 02:22 UTC: SRE alert for throughput drop; rollback of the most recent config change (batch-window-tuning) executed — no recovery.
- 2025-11-03 02:40–03:30 UTC: Multiple Canary runs; intermittent recovery when a single client sends fixed-length requests, fails for long-chat blends.
- 2025-11-03 04:00 UTC: Identified increased prefill queue occupancy and higher kv-cache miss rates for small prefixes.

Key telemetry snapshots (approx):
- Baseline tokens/sec (model-x-4k): 1.2M 
- During regression: 780k
- Prefill queue depth: baseline 12 -> regressed 34 average
- KVCache hit-rate for prefix keys: baseline 91% -> regressed 68%
- p50 latency: +8%
- p95 latency: +22%
- p99 latency: +150% (short bursts)

Important logs (snippets):
- from prefill worker stderr (2025-11-03T02:37:48Z):
  "W prefiller.cc:284] delayed_schedule(): window count mismatch, expected 16 got 9, rescheduling"
- from batcher metrics (2025-11-03T02:40:02Z):
  "INFO batcher:evict: eviction_policy:LRU, candidate_count=24, slots_freed=0 -> slot-starvation?"
- from kvcache (2025-11-03T02:41:11Z):
  "I kv_cache.cpp:102] lookup_many: requested 128 keys, returned 40 hits, 88 misses, backing-lookup-took=12ms"
- repeated error seen occasionally: "E slot_allocator: allocate_batch: allocation failed for size=256, free_slots=0"

Commands and quick experiments executed (ordered):
1) Replayed local synthetic steadyflow (small-medium-long mix) against staging cluster to reproduce:
   - command: ./loadgen --profile mixed_chat --rps 500 --model model-x-4k --seqdist long-heavy
   - result: reproduction ✅, tokens/sec down ~28% relative to baseline run.

2) Enabled debug logging for batcher and prefiller on a single node:
   - edits: /etc/redwood/runtime/conf.d/batcher.toml log_level=DEBUG; prefiller.log_level=DEBUG
   - tail: journalctl -u redwood-batcher -f
   - observation: "pack attempts frequently reduced to 1 or 2 items despite window size configured to 16"

3) Forcing kvcache warming for prefix lengths <=8 to test hit-rate effect:
   - script used: tools/kv_warmup.py --model model-x-4k --prefix-lens 1-8 --concurrency 8
   - result: kvcache hit-rate rose to ~84% and tokens/sec recovered ~15% temporarily, p99 spikes reduced.
   - interpretation: kvcache misses amplify packing inefficiency; prefill path spends more time fetching from backing store and delays batch closure.

4) Flipping the new batching heuristic feature-flag (batcher.prefill_heuristic_v2=false) on a test node:
   - via runtime-agent API: POST /node/flags {prefill_heuristic_v2:false}
   - result: immediate stabilization of batch sizes to expected distribution on that node and throughput back to ~95% baseline for that node; cluster-level still degraded.

5) Tried shrinking max_window_size from 32 -> 12 in a canary config:
   - result: reduced queue depth but overall tokens/sec still below baseline; latency improved for short requests only.

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Regression in heuristic_v2 that interacts poorly with kvcache miss patterns (main candidate). Evidence: flipping flag helps per-node, warmup improves throughput.
B) Slot allocator starvation when eviction_policy fails to free slots under mixed-length workloads. Evidence: 'slots_freed=0' log and allocation fails.
C) Prefill scheduling race that causes windows to be split incorrectly ("window count mismatch" messages). Evidence: observed warnings and reduced pack attempts.
D) Backing-store latency regression (DB/redis) periodically causing prefill slowdowns. Evidence: backing-lookup-took=12ms — high but not catastrophic; could be compounding.

Notes on each hypothesis and how to test further:
- A (heuristic_v2 + kvcache): run a controlled A/B on 10 nodes (v2 on/off) with identical load mix, gather per-node batch-size distribution, prefill waits, and kvcache hit rates. If v2 nodes show lower batch sizes and higher misses, we can bisect code changes in the last PR (linked PR in artifacts).

- B (slot allocator): reproduce with high slot pressure toy workload that forces many concurrent unique prefixes; enable slot allocator traces (ALLOC_TRACE=1) and inspect eviction decisions. Try toggling eviction_policy to "aggressive" to force frees. If freeing solves throughput, follow up with improved eviction heuristics.

- C (prefill scheduling race): add additional instrumentation around prefill->schedule boundary (timestamping, window_id). If mismatches correspond to certain request shapes (e.g., long prefix then short continuation), then scheduling bug likely.

- D (backing-store): measure backing store percentiles under load; replicate miss handling with synthetic slow-redis to see if similar throughput drop.

Quick wins attempted so far (and outcomes):
- Warmed kvcache for small prefixes: partial recovery (~15%).
- Disabled prefill_heuristic_v2 on a node: that node recovered.
- Shortened max_window_size on canary: partial latency improvement only.

Edge clues I don't want to ignore:
- The regression surfaced right after a config push that touched batcher window defaults and also rolled out heuristic_v2 to 60% of nodes. The timing implicates both changes — could be an interaction.
- We see more "allocate_batch: allocation failed" on nodes with more concurrent small-prefix traffic (supporting slot allocator theory).
- GPU kernels and driver logs show no errors; memory pressure not elevated.

Next concrete steps (short list):
1) Run A/B on 12 nodes (6 with prefill_heuristic_v2 true, 6 false) under the mixed-chat profile; collect: per-node batch-size histogram, kvcache hit/miss, prefill wait histograms, allocator free-slot counts. (Owner: me, ETA 2025-11-06)
2) Add temporary ALLOC_TRACE to reproduce slot frees on one canary node and force eviction_policy=aggressive to test rescue. (Owner: Marco, ETA 2025-11-06)
3) Add minimal timestamp instrumentation at prefill schedule boundary and deploy to test cluster to capture window_id mismatches. (Owner: Eleni, ETA 2025-11-07)
4) If A above confirms heuristic_v2 as primary, revert to v1 cluster-wide and open a deeper bisect PR for v2. (Owner: me, ETA after A/B)

Scratchpad commands (copyable):
- loadgen: ./loadgen --profile mixed_chat --rps 500 --model model-x-4k --seqdist long-heavy
- enable node flag: curl -X POST "http://node-agent.local/flags" -d '{"prefill_heuristic_v2": false}'
- kv warmup: python tools/kv_warmup.py --model model-x-4k --prefix-lens 1-8 --concurrency 8 --endpoint staging.cluster
- collect traces: ssh node-3 && sudo journalctl -u redwood-prefiller -o cat --since "2025-11-03 02:00" > /tmp/prefill-trace.log

Loose observations / brain-dump:
- I suspect heuristic_v2 introduced a threshold that defers packing when KV hit-rate below x, but that threshold wasn't adaptive to request-shape diversity, so in mixed workloads it keeps opening new windows instead of packing, increasing queue depth and starvation.
- If true, a short-term mitigation is to make the threshold conservative (favor packing) until v2 is revisited.
- Long term: we need a simple offline corpus-based sim (loadgen replay + offline batcher) to validate packing heuristics across request mixes. Add to Optimize backlog.

Unresolved questions:
- Why does kvcache miss-rate change abruptly? Are clients altering prefix distributions or did the cache eviction policy silently change?
- Is there any cross-node state (global counts) that could cause coordinated misbehavior?

If you pick this up: follow the Next concrete steps, paste any new logs into this doc, and call me (Riya) if you flip flags cluster-wide so I can coordinate experiments.

End of noisy journal entry. Will summarize into a concise incident follow-up once A/B results are in.
